'''Utsunomiya Shrine''' (宇都宮神社) is a [[Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine}}]] located in [[Komaki|Komaki, Aichi}}]], [[Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture}}]]. The shrine is notable for being the site of one of the largest [[zenpō-kōhō-fun|Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}]] in the Owari region, known as the '''Utsunomiya Shrine Kofun'''.

== History ==
* Late [[3rd century|3rd century}}]] to early [[4th century|4th century}}]] - built of the [[zenpō-kōhō-fun|Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}]].
* Around [[1929|1929}}]] (Showa 4) - Discovery of a [[Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror]].
* [[September 9, 1987]] (Showa 62) - The kofun was Historic Site1 a [[Historic Site of Aichi Prefecture]], and the mirror was Historic Site1 a [[designation1 of Aichi Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.aichi.jp/kyoiku/bunka/bunkazainavi/yukei/kouko/kensitei/0733.html|title=Triangular-rimmed deity-and-beast mirror|publisher=Aichi Prefecture|accessdate=2013-05-22}}</ref>

== Utsunomiya Shrine Kofun ==
{{Infobox ancient site
| name = Utsunomiya Shrine Kofun

Located within the grounds of Utsunomiya Shrine, this is one of the largest [[zenpō-kōhō-fun|Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}]] in the Owari region. Part of the [[Koki Kofun Cluster]], it was constructed in the late [[3rd century|3rd century}}]] to early [[4th century|4th century}}]]. The presence of the kofun indicates the prominence of a powerful local clan during that era. In addition to this kofun, several others exist in the vicinity. The mound is 59m in total length, 6.5m in height, and approximately 35m on each side of the rear section. A vertical stone chamber is located within. The site was Historic Site1 a Historic Site of Aichi Prefecture in [[1987|1987}}]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.aichi.jp/kyoiku/bunka/bunkazainavi/kinenbutu/siseki/kensitei/0923.html|title=Utsunomiya Shrine Kofun|publisher=Aichi Prefecture|accessdate=2013-05-22}}</ref>

== Historic Site ==
* Triangular-rimmed deity-and-beast mirror (三角縁獣文帯三神三獣鏡) - A [[Bronze mirror|Bronze mirror}}]] excavated from the Utsunomiya Shrine Kofun. It was discovered around [[1929|1929}}]] during the construction of the shrine hall at the front of the kofun and Historic Site1 a designation1 of Aichi Prefecture in [[1987|1987}}]].

== location ==
[[Komaki|Komaki, Aichi}}]], Ogi 3-chome 226.

== Access ==
* 5-minute walk from the [[Ogi bus stop]] served by [[Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus}}]].
